title: Decatur Street joints and horse-race jobs with Octave Crosby
summary: Decatur Street had four-piece bands nightly; at the racetrack the band played between races for Crosby.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: It's got two little melodies in there. What about Decatur Street? I think you mentioned something about that one still playing over there. Oh yeah. Decatur Street one time was just like Boydham Street. It wasn't Boydham Street, it was Decatur Street. Everything was on Decatur Street. They had joints with three, four piece bands. And then, that was every night. Did you ever work at Popeyes or Kingsbury? Yeah. Around those places? Oh, I worked in other places around there. I don't remember working at Popeyes or Cape. I played there maybe one night. But, yeah, so many other places. I played other places around there. And that was every night. Did you play a lot of blues there? Blues. Just mix them up. Mostly, mostly jump numbers, you know, Dix and Lab. Lively numbers. Did you have shows there? Dances? No. No. Just had a four piece band there. Just play for them. Oh, what's it like when you go off to play for these horse races? That's another thing on this, you know. You know, the freakness of the dirt. What happens up there? Well, you mean what the band or how the band do or what? Yeah, what do they do? Do they have a dance or do you play for the horses? No, they just have us out there and we play between the horses. Play a number of in between the races. And, well, we got out there before to play a dance the night before. Like the race is on Saturday, we got out there to play a dance on Friday. They have loud speakers set up there at the racetrack so that people can hear you or you just play loud? Well, we just play, we just play loud because most of the time they have us on a floor or something and moving around. Moving all around the field, different spots. Whose band are you up there with? Octave Crosby. It's always Octave, huh? Octave Crosby. Octave Crosby. Well, it was Bill Matthews. It wasn't Bill Matthews on the job, but now we saw Dave Crosby. I don't remember if Papa went up there or not. I mean, tell us to him. I don't believe.
